B scores highest at 0.24, ahead of D and E at 0.18, so selecting the top one node by PageRank selects B, drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Computes a centrality score for every node, ranks the nodes from highest to lowest score, and selects the top `k`. It combines a centrality computation and a selection step in one call, so the most important nodes can be acted on directly with the `*_ws` methods. Typical uses: - highlighting or labelling the most influential nodes before plotting - extracting the core of a network with `transform_to_subgraph_ws()` - targeted-attack robustness experiments, deleting the top hubs with `delete_nodes_ws()` and measuring how the graph falls apart The measures differ in what "important" means: degree counts direct connections, PageRank rewards links from other important nodes, and betweenness rewards nodes that sit on many shortest paths. Degree-based measures are cheap; betweenness computes all-pairs shortest paths and can be slow on large graphs. The scores are only used for ranking; no node attribute is written. The nodes are added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [measure]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["degree"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Centrality measure used for ranking. One of `"degree"` (default; total degree, i.e. in-degree plus out-degree for directed graphs, as returned by `get_degree()`), `"in_degree"` or `"out_degree"` (directed graphs only; `ValueError` otherwise), `"pagerank"` (see `pagerank()`), or `"betweenness"` (see `betweenness_centrality()`). Any other value raises `ValueError`. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of top-ranked nodes to select. Defaults to `10`. If `k` is at least the number of nodes, every node is selected; `k=0` selects nothing. [include_ties]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Controls what happens when several nodes share the score at the cut-off. If `False` (default), exactly `k` nodes are selected and ties at the boundary are broken arbitrarily, so which of the tied nodes is chosen is not guaranteed. If `True`, every node whose score is at least the `k`-th highest score is selected, so the result can contain more than `k` nodes. [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How the selected nodes combine with the current node selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected nodes among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. Any edge selection is cleared, since the graph holds a selection of nodes or of edges but not both. [**kwargs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Extra keyword arguments forwarded to `pagerank()` (e.g., `damping=`, `max_iter=`, `tol=`) or `betweenness_centrality()` (`weighted=`). An argument the chosen measure doesn't accept, any argument for the degree measures, and `attr_name=` / `return_dict=` (nothing is stored) raise `TypeError`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `measure=` is unknown, if `"in_degree"` or `"out_degree"` is used on an undirected graph, or if `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this graph "A" has degree `3`, "B" and "C" are tied at `2`, and "D" has degree `1`. Asking for the top two by degree selects "A" plus one of the tied pair, so the count is exactly `2`: ::: {#5c9ba238 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C")]) .select_nodes_by_centrality("degree", k=2) ) graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: With `include_ties=True`, both "B" and "C" are kept because they share the score at the cut-off, so the selection grows to three nodes and is deterministic: ::: {#91e6b260 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.select_nodes_by_centrality("degree", k=2, include_ties=True) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C'] ``` ::: ::: Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to `pagerank()` -- here `damping=` is passed through. In this directed graph every other node links to "hub", so it ranks first: ::: {#cd7b89c8 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} web = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["hub", "p1", "p2", "p3"]) .add_edges([("p1", "hub"), ("p2", "hub"), ("p3", "hub"), ("hub", "p1")]) .select_nodes_by_centrality("pagerank", k=1, damping=0.85) ) [web.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in web.get_selected_node_ids()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['hub'] ``` ::: ::: The scores are only used for ranking and aren't stored on the nodes. To keep them, run the measure itself: ::: {#3c9db366 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} web.pagerank(damping=0.85).get_node_df().select("label", "pagerank") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
